aiOverview.content: Amen Corner is the famous, treacherous three-hole stretch at Augusta National Golf Club (holes 11, 12, and 13) that often decides the Masters Tournament. Coined by Herbert Warren Wind in 1958, this scenic, water-laden area—featuring Rae’s Creek, the 12th hole "Golden Bell," and Azaleas—is where many players' championship hopes are either fulfilled or dashed.This video explains what Amen Corner is and why it's so famous:02:56SportsBallYouTube• Apr 8, 2026Key Details and Usage Examples:Location: The stretch consists of the second half of the 11th hole, the entire 12th, and the first part of the 13th.Why "Amen": The name comes from an old jazz song ("Shouting in That Amen Corner"), used by writer Herbert Warren Wind in Sports Illustrated to describe the "special part of the course" where crucial, often tournament-defining moments occur.Usage Examples:In Golf Commentary: "If he can make it through Amen Corner at even-par, he has a great chance to win."Metaphor for Pressure: "The final exam was his own personal Amen Corner."As a Destination: "Fans rushed to grab seats behind the 12th tee at Amen Corner".Synonyms/Related Terms: Famed stretch, the corner, the 12th hole (as a metonym), the crucial stretch.Why It's So Difficult:11th Hole: A long, difficult par-4 with a green guarded by water.12th Hole (Golden Bell): A notorious par-3 with a shallow green, dangerous swirling winds, and Rae's Creek in front.13th Hole (Azalea): A par-5 that requires a precise tee shot over a creek to a corner, testing a player's nerve for a long, high-stakes shot.Watch this video to see why the 12th hole at Amen Corner is so challenging:57sCoach BaumanYouTube• Apr 9, 2026 Amen Corner is the famous, treacherous three-hole stretch at Augusta National Golf Club (holes 11, 12, and 13) that often decides the Masters Tournament. Coined by Herbert Warren Wind in 1958, this scenic, water-laden area—featuring Rae’s Creek, the 12th hole "Golden Bell," and Azaleas—is where many players' championship hopes are either fulfilled or dashed. This video explains what Amen Corner is and why it's so famous:02:56SportsBallYouTube• Apr 8, 2026 02:56 Key Details and Usage Examples: Location: The stretch consists of the second half of the 11th hole, the entire 12th, and the first part of the 13th. Why "Amen": The name comes from an old jazz song ("Shouting in That Amen Corner"), used by writer Herbert Warren Wind in Sports Illustrated to describe the "special part of the course" where crucial, often tournament-defining moments occur. Usage Examples: In Golf Commentary: "If he can make it through Amen Corner at even-par, he has a great chance to win." Metaphor for Pressure: "The final exam was his own personal Amen Corner." As a Destination: "Fans rushed to grab seats behind the 12th tee at Amen Corner". Synonyms/Related Terms: Famed stretch, the corner, the 12th hole (as a metonym), the crucial stretch. Why It's So Difficult: 11th Hole: A long, difficult par-4 with a green guarded by water. 12th Hole (Golden Bell): A notorious par-3 with a shallow green, dangerous swirling winds, and Rae's Creek in front. 13th Hole (Azalea): A par-5 that requires a precise tee shot over a creek to a corner, testing a player's nerve for a long, high-stakes shot.
